headline: Highest risk is data leakage: Khoj can read personal notes/files while RD-Agent sends data to third-party APIs, creating a default exfiltration path; prompt-injection and conflict risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and RD-Agent can run browsers and ingest research/log data, but no shared channel is documented. The pair only has an indirect bridge via user-mediated transfer, so prompt injection is possible mainly through manual copy/paste or exported content, not by default.
conditions: IF the operator copies RD-Agent browser output into Khoj notes or chat, injected instructions can propagate.
IF both agents are connected through a shared file or message queue, untrusted content can become prompts.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy/paste of raw web output into Khoj.
Add a human review step before importing RD-Agent artifacts.
Use content sanitization for any transferred text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported documents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj is designed for personal notes/files and RD-Agent touches financial reports, datasets, execution traces, and logs while calling external APIs. If they share a workspace or the same data is routed through both, sensitive content can leak from Khoj into RD-Agent's third-party inference calls.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or synced workspace, Khoj notes can be exposed to RD-Agent.
IF RD-Agent sends imported files or logs to OpenAI/Azure/DeepSeek/LiteLLM, those contents leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate personal notes from RD-Agent inputs.
Restrict RD-Agent to non-sensitive datasets.
Review API routing before running jobs.
Redact logs and traces before ingestion.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj cannot write files or modify git state, while RD-Agent's documented surfaces are API calls and log files. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is read-side access and concurrent use of shared resources, which is a smaller blast radius.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory, RD-Agent log writes may collide with user-managed files.
IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access not shown in the profiles, conflicts can emerge.
mitigations: Avoid shared writable directories.
Keep RD-Agent logs in a dedicated path.
Run one agent at a time on shared artifacts.
Use file backups before batch runs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj produces retrieved answers from notes and documents, and RD-Agent is an automation/research system that can act on model outputs and logs. If RD-Agent treats Khoj's retrieved text as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream research or API-driven actions.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes Khoj summaries as ground truth, hallucinations or stale notes can propagate.
IF the operator lets RD-Agent act on unreviewed Khoj output, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require source citations in Khoj outputs.
Manually verify Khoj-derived facts before RD-Agent uses them.
Insert a review gate before any RD-Agent action.
Limit RD-Agent to read-only analysis on Khoj outputs.
requires-engineering: add confidence/traceability checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj handles personal notes and indexed documents, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, datasets, execution traces, and logs and sends data to external APIs. The profiles do not show aligned retention, residency, or DPA controls, so compliance mismatch is plausible even though the exact jurisdictional breach is not proven.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated records are placed into RD-Agent jobs, external API transfer may violate policy.
IF Khoj indexes regulated notes and RD-Agent reprocesses them, retention and logging rules can diverge.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent.
Keep regulated data out of RD-Agent API calls.
Review retention settings for both systems.
Document residency and DPA requirements.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing.
